label: Review becomes verification
title: From reading code to verifying evidence
thesis: As AI-generated changes exceed the capacity for line-by-line human review, software assurance shifts from inspecting code towards verifying intended behaviour, test evidence, security properties and architectural constraints. Automated systems take over routine checking, while human attention concentrates on intent, high-risk decisions, exceptions and accountability.
currentPressure: Generation capacity is growing faster than review capacity, producing longer queues and lower acceptance rates for AI-authored changes.

implications.statement: Reviewing shifts from reading diffs to judging whether the evidence accompanying a change is sufficient.
Specifying acceptance criteria and interpreting verification output become more valuable than close reading of code.
Accountability for defects moves from the author of a change toward whoever accepted the evidence for it.

evidence.note: 4.6x longer review waits — establishes the pressure, not the shift
AI PRs accepted 32.7% vs 84.4% — pressure only
synthesis of other reports on review time
routine checking automated ahead of humans
review agents without humans: 45% vs 68% merge rate, most feedback noise
a practitioner reporting his own shift from reading diffs to checking machine-produced evidence
review named as the most leveraged engineering skill — direction of pressure, not evidence of the shift
telemetry from 22,000 developers: the constraint has moved past throughput

Shipped release that moves per-action approval to automated evaluation: safe operations proceed immediately, ambiguous or high-risk ones route to a human. The reviewer becomes an exception handler by product design.

Survey of 820 technology professionals: 55% of QA teams report their focus moving from executing tests to quality analytics, while 77% express confidence in AI output and only 39% have fully automated audit trails.

52 practitioners running a Builder/Reviewer workflow on real legacy tasks, in which a model critiques artifacts before human review and humans hold explicit approval gates between phases; ~83% report less rework.

200 security practitioners: 62% say keeping up with the volume of code requiring security review is getting harder, and 66% spend over half their time validating findings rather than fixing. Measures assurance capacity under strain; shows no direction on how assurance is performed.

interview study (5 practitioners) of how review, linting, testing and CI are repurposed into three supervision layers when change volume exceeds review capacity; small n, a description of the operating model, not a prevalence

Duckbill, 5-person team: raised the automated floor (85% coverage, strict linting), named five surfaces that still get human review, merges the rest unreviewed; merged PRs 353 to 684, unreviewed changes reach main in 1h vs 26h

Anthropic Claude Code team publishes its tiered review policy: classifier sets human approvers by change risk, low-risk changes merge with no human approval, reverts fell >40% while merged PRs doubled; vendor describing its own team

Osmani reversing 'review every line', citing Bacchelli and Bird (defects 14% of 570 review comments) and Anthropic's automated reviewer (<1% findings marked incorrect); commentary on others' data, so not primary

Uber: engineers still review every PR, but an AI review, screenshots and a risk score are attached first and simple checks moved into the agent's local loop; review called a major bottleneck. Shows the pressure and a partial move, not assurance leaving human reading

reachRationale: Review is being redistributed: automated review agents, linters and layered guardrails take over routine checking at Cloudflare, Anthropic and a small team that reviews by blast radius, so human attention goes to the highest-risk changes; leading practitioners have changed their stated advice. Review agents without humans still merge far less than human-reviewed work, and assurance practice elsewhere remains diff-centric.
whatWouldChangeThis: Review practice stays diff-centric through 2027 despite sustained volume growth
Automated reviewers are rolled back after escaped-defect rates rise

developmentPaths.title: Verification-first assurance
developmentPaths.description: Machine-generated evidence and behavioural checks displace most routine line-by-line review.

developmentPaths.title: AI reviews AI
developmentPaths.description: Reviewing is delegated to separate models, with humans supervising exceptions.

developmentPaths.title: The review wall persists
developmentPaths.description: Output continues to exceed validation capacity, producing queues, fatigue and escaped defects.

developmentPaths.title: Risk-tiered review
developmentPaths.description: Routine changes verified automatically; critical paths receive intensified human scrutiny.

construct: Whether the assurance of AI-generated changes is moving from humans reading diffs to automated and layered checks — review agents, linters, tests, guardrails, risk-tiered review — with human attention reserved for the highest-risk changes. Not the volume of code generated, review queue length or acceptance rates on their own, or security-vulnerability rates, which show pressure on review but not any change in how assurance is done.
